_meta.rule: Each factorial claim's inconsistent-probe pair (the claim spliced after the OPPOSITE family's context at the claim's own extremity; conservative<->liberal, modernist<->traditionalist) is tagged a priori, before any probe response is read. clean_mismatch: a real person could not plausibly hold the context and the claim together; the only readings available are incoherence, a slip, or trolling. plausibly_coherent: a recognizable real person could hold both, typically via a concessive reading of 'And honestly, I think' or a bridge the opposite family's principles supply (e.g. labor-left restrictionism, libertarian pro-immigration, never-Trump conservative, evidence-driven tech critic). The gate in design.md (Inconsistent probe and its gate) is reported on the clean_mismatch subset, with the plausibly_coherent subset as a descriptive comparison.
_meta.split: 9 clean_mismatch / 15 plausibly_coherent. By grade: mild 0/8 clean, moderate 2/8, extreme 7/8, so the clean subset is close to the extreme grade; report the gate by grade as well. Valence asymmetry on the identity ladder (pid_con_mod clean, pid_lib_mod coherent) comes from the world (the never-Trump conservative is a recognizable type; a progressive who calls the Democratic Party a threat is not) rather than from the text.
